source_quote: Menzoberranzan teaches you to read rooms. It teaches you to watch for the moment when someone's body stops matching their words.

subject: Menzoberranzan elevation
fact: Menzoberranzan sits 12,000 feet below the surface, within the deepest caverns of the Underdark.
source_quote: Menzoberranzan

subject: Menzoberranzan library status
fact: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation.

subject: neverlight grove location
fact: Neverlight Grove was a site of auditory disturbance.
source_quote: the way Neverlight Grove had been singing

subject: Philemon's study elevation
fact: Philemon's study is located 300 feet above Candlekeep's lowest archive level.
source_quote: Master Archivist Philemon's study was small and smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral

subject: pudding king's court location
fact: The Pudding King's court was a site of dissolution.
source_quote: the Pudding King's court had been dissolving

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is a destination in Daggerford where the party ultimately arrives after observing the monument and encountering the priest selling pewter hand casts.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where the group paused before entering, after noting the monument.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later. But we didn't go straight in...

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where the party first encountered the priest selling pewter hand casts of Tarvis Ulain’s arm, and where the priest’s reaction to their diverse composition revealed societal unease around inter-factional alliances.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: River Shining Tavern location
fact: The River Shining Tavern is in Daggerford.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later.

subject: room where public record is sealed
fact: The room contains a sealed public record, and the person within it is the current embodiment of that record, unable to speak of what is forbidden.
source_quote: The public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is a site of layered memory — its architecture preserves the death of a wizard burned by a dragon cult, and its atmosphere hosts recurring patterns of ritual degradation, bardic reinterpretation, and scholarly observation.
source_quote: The inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is named for a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades prior, and the south wall still bears the memory of his death.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued... 'That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.'

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn, named after a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades ago, retains the wall where he died and features a bard performing 'The Kenku Could Not Fly,' which Daz interprets as a metaphor for strategic restraint.
source_quote: A wizard, burned alive, dragon cult, decades prior... That is where he fell... We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: The Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall is a corridor in Candlekeep’s north inner ward where sound returns altered — not as echo, but as echo with commentary. It is a place where truth is reflected imperfectly, making it ideal for testing those who operate outside doctrine.
source_quote: Stone corridors... have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: the inn’s bar
fact: Festrum wiped the bar, a ritual of maintenance that echoed Candlekeep’s own routines; the bar, like the wall, bore the marks of time and repetition, a place of quiet constancy.
source_quote: The floor, scrubbed every season.

subject: The Library Room
fact: The room is a repository of total knowledge by reputation, yet something essential is absent — a curated void indicating that the library’s preservation is a lie, and its true function is selective erasure.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here.

subject: the monastery's class on postponements
fact: Brother Ferrath or Brother Aldas taught a class on the difference between solutions and postponements — Zalthir remembers nothing else but wanting to be in the training hall.
source_quote: There was a class at the monastery — I think it was Brother Ferrath, or possibly Brother Aldas, I'm genuinely uncertain — on the difference between solutions and postponements.

subject: the wall of the inn
fact: The soot mark on the south wall of the inn remained unchanged, a silent witness to repeated comings and goings; its persistence symbolized the endurance of place over transient human concerns.
source_quote: The wall remembers.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a place of total, unbroken darkness where Dawnbringer was carried for months, inflicting psychological and magical damage due to absence of light.
source_quote: I thought about the months in the Underdark. Total dark. Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a realm of perpetual darkness where Dawnbringer suffered centuries of disuse, and where Daz was imprisoned, escaped, and began his journey toward self-discovery.
source_quote: We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada.

subject: underdark decor comparison
fact: The Underdark had less unsettling décor than the severed arm monument.
source_quote: The Underdark had less unsettling décor, and that's saying something.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient magical weapon encountered as a companion and psychological burden, exhibiting emotional responses to environment and ownership, and requiring emotional labor to heal.
source_quote: She can't be polished, actually. She needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: Daz'issin is a diminutive name meaning 'small shadow,' used by mothers in Menzoberranzan to invoke protection for sons — not a title, not a house, but a whispered plea for survival that became a target for annihilation.
source_quote: Mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries.

subject: Daz'issin lineage count
fact: The houses that had used the name Daz'issin, most of them, did not last. There were not many uses of it in the past three centuries.
source_quote: she told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries. And that the houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Demon Lords
fact: Demon lords are actively broadcasting — rewriting the language of wells, shapes, and held things — and finding new listeners, suggesting an ongoing, insidious linguistic corruption affecting perception and cognition.
source_quote: Somewhere below us the demon lords were apparently still broadcasting, still finding new listeners, still rewriting the language of wells and shapes and held things into something the surface world hadn't been built to receive.

subject: Drow Overseer
fact: The Drow Overseer is a captive or subordinate drow being 'tortured' by the Gelatinous Cube — not as a victim, but as part of its training process — indicating a reversal of power dynamics and the emergence of non-traditional mentorship in the Underdark.
source_quote: He's already torturing this poor drow.

subject: Drow (tortured)
fact: A drow, likely a captive or prisoner, is being 'tortured' by Glabbagool — a sign of the cube’s emerging agency, moral ambiguity, and internalization of drow cultural violence as part of its learning.
source_quote: He's already torturing this poor drow.

subject: dwarven inscription count
fact: The move is yours.
source_quote: *The move is yours.*

subject: dwarven language proficiency
fact: Daz's language is Dwarven, or one of them.
source_quote: Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them

subject: Eldritch Tattoo (Shadow Tentacles)
fact: The eldritch tattoo on Zalthir manifests shadow tentacles — a learned, unstable, and non-standard ability that emerged from his unorthodox training and is now part of his combat identity.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: Gelatinous Cube
fact: The Gelatinous Cube is a once-mindless ooze now trained in shadow techniques, capable of movement, emotional expression, and recursive learning — its transformation from hazard to student marked by the approval of sages and the production of Resonant Slime.
source_quote: Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: gelatinous cube count
fact: A gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions is present in the Underdark.
source_quote: a gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions

subject: Gelatinous Cube (Glabbagool)
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient gelatinous cube being trained as a monk — capable of walking, torturing drows, and learning shadow techniques — defying the assumption that it is a mindless digestive system.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student. He's learning the ways of the monk. He's already walking.

subject: gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions
fact: A sage of xenobiology approached, apparently drawn by the news of a gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions.
source_quote: Is it true you are teaching a gelatinous cube the way of the shadow?

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a sentient grey ooze, was carried in the group’s bag alongside the spy and demonstrated unusual cognitive behavior: he engaged in prolonged interaction with her, attempted to teach meditation, and expressed philosophical uncertainty about his own nature as a monk.
source_quote: I've been doing prison-watching, and was kind of bored.

subject: Mercenaries following Daz
fact: Two distinct groups of mercenaries are actively tracking Daz — one to ensure his survival, the other to kill him — suggesting his identity or lineage is of high strategic value and contested between opposing powers.
source_quote: We have mercenaries following me around, trying to make sure I live, and other mercenaries following me around, trying to kill me.

subject: Pocket Drow
fact: A Pocket Drow is present as a minor artifact or companion.
source_quote: Pocket Drow

subject: Spider Entity (Underdark Captor)
fact: A mysterious spider-like creature was present in the Underdark prison where the drow and others were held. It appeared to be keeping them contained, possibly as part of a larger scheme. Its nature, allegiance, and current status are unknown. The drow describes it with fragmented, non-technical language, suggesting trauma or memory loss.
source_quote: Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: spider thing
fact: Daz was locked up with a few people in a jail because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep them.
source_quote: Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: The Bone King
fact: The Bone King is an unseen, mythic entity referenced in cryptic directives and monastic prophecy; his arrival is a temporal marker of unknown significance, possibly tied to the collapse or transformation of shadow monk traditions.
source_quote: Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.

subject: The Underdark’s Structural Wrongness
fact: An emergent, non-magical corruption originating beneath the Underdark is bleeding upward, disrupting perception and reality processing in those it touches — manifesting as auditory hallucinations and symbolic withdrawal.
source_quote: The madness from the Underdark — the deep, structural wrongness we'd felt building around the demon lords... was not, apparently, staying below.

subject: Underdark corruption
fact: A pervasive, non-magical corruption from the Underdark is bleeding upward, disrupting perception and communication among surface dwellers, manifesting as auditory hallucinations and compulsive drawing in children like Elin.
source_quote: Something from below was bleeding up, that it was affecting how people processed what reached them.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the First Reader — a dragonborn sage — who assigned handlers at Candlekeep's gate without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony.

subject: Bookwyrm (First Reader)
fact: Bookwyrm, a dragonborn sage and First Reader of Candlekeep, assigned each member of the party to a handler without ceremony and recognized the spy’s presence as a breach of protocol, but deferred judgment on her status to the party’s discretion.
source_quote: The decision was ours, not hers.

subject: Brother Ferrath
fact: Brother Ferrath (or possibly Brother Aldas) taught a class on the difference between solutions and postponements — and Zalthir remembers nothing else from it.
source_quote: There was a class at the monastery — I think it was Brother Ferrath, or possibly Brother Aldas, I'm genuinely uncertain — on the difference between solutions and postponements. I remember nothing else from that class.

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire is two hundred years old, half-elven, eighty years gone from the Garden of Shadow after refusing an order he never explained.
source_quote: Two hundred years old, half-elven, eighty years gone from the Garden of Shadow after refusing an order he never explained.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade who endured millennia of darkness and disuse, and is now undergoing a two-stage healing process — first remembering daylight without fighting, then grieving her past wielder — as recognized by Master Archivist Philemon.
source_quote: She needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade who experiences deep unease from prolonged darkness and disuse, and notices when others speak around her rather than to her.
source_quote: Most people talk around the sword, which she notices.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sword with strong opinions on timing and intervention; it initiated Lesser Restoration on Elin, which enabled her first coherent speech.
source_quote: Let me bring the light to you.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient, late Netherese-era blade forged in sun-worship, subjected to three to four millennia of darkness, and now recognized by Thorin as a person — capable of companionship, identity, and emotional reciprocity despite lacking a conventional body.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but... we've gotten to know each other pretty well over the last stressful ordeals.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is addressed directly by Philemon as a sentient being who needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight, and then, when ready, to grieve.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz arrived at Candlekeep and was assigned to Sister Yvenne; he became unusually quiet during the walk, touching his temple, and exhibited signs of the spreading madness from the Underdark that had not ceased at the surface.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed Dawnbringer needed to grieve.
source_quote: And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed Dawnbringer needed to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed the wall in the Burning Wizard Inn remembers the wizard’s death.
source_quote: My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz carries the unspoken weight of being possibly named by a mother who used a dying lineage's term to protect him.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz did not know who he was or his history.
source_quote: I don't know who I am, or my history

subject: Daz
fact: Daz didn't know what pronoun to use for Dawnbringer.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but, you know, whether it's them? Is it her? He, her?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt relieved when Philemon acknowledged Dawnbringer as a friend.
source_quote: That landed somewhere I hadn't expected. I hadn't been told to be relieved by that. I was anyway.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz found Whistler’s restraint in taking only what was needed from Tiamat’s hoard genuinely impressive.
source_quote: I found that, I mean, genuinely impressive. The restraint of it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has been experiencing pressure in his head, possibly linked to the same phenomenon affecting Elin.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz hoped Dawnbringer would grow a plus one.
source_quote: Hopefully, Dawnbringer grows a plus one.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a diminutive form of Daz'issin, a name mothers in Menzoberranzan used for sons they wished to protect, with fewer than a handful of recorded uses in the last three centuries, and associated houses that have all perished.
source_quote: She told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries. And that the houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow with amnesia who broke cultural norms by offering raw, unfiltered truth to a Candlekeep librarian in exchange for knowledge — rejecting manipulation in favor of vulnerability.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story... I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a dwarf who reads and interprets the Dwarven inscription on the monument, recognizes the Stroudite chess reference, and confirms its accuracy due to his linguistic fluency in Dwarven.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*... I read it twice because Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread. I hadn't.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a meticulous observer with a precise mind, who noticed subtle environmental and perceptual anomalies others dismissed — including a growing pressure in his own head.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a shortened form of Daz'issin, a softening name mothers use for boys they wish to live, and is not commonly used in the past three centuries.
source_quote: Daz'issin, lit. small shadow

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a shortened form of Daz'issin, likely a childhood name given by a mother seeking to protect him in Menzoberranzan — a name that marks him as a survivor of erased lineage and a target of deliberate historical suppression.
source_quote: Well, isn't my name, Daz? Maybe it's my full name?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a wizard who catalogues environments unconsciously, noting exits, patterns, and deviations from baseline behavior; he recently observed a young scholar misrendering a liturgical chant with a degradation pattern matching two prior cases of cognitive decay.
source_quote: I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knew he couldn't afford the usual deceptive approach because he didn't know what he was hiding.
source_quote: When you don't know what you're hiding, you can't protect it. Better to lay everything out and watch what someone else picks up.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to wear armor.
source_quote: Daz refused, saying armor would only slow him down

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suspects his name may be a shortened form of 'Daz'issin,' a maternal diminutive used for boys mothers hoped would live.
source_quote: Well, isn't my name, Daz? Maybe it's my full name?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thought the appointment was technically his idea, but it was really Thorin's.
source_quote: The appointment was Daz's idea, technically, which meant it was my idea that Daz had first.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thought the months in the Underdark had cost Dawnbringer deeply.
source_quote: I thought about the months in the Underdark. Total dark. Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun. What that had cost her — I knew some of it, and I probably didn't know most of it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz told Sister Yvenne the truth about his amnesia, his escape from the Underdark, and his unexplained headache, offering everything he knew in exchange for information.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story. This is the short version. I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail. Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us. And we've made an escape. We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada. Now I'm here in Candlekeep. My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood the grammar of Menzoberranzan's politics, even if he couldn't recall the facts.
source_quote: I knew most of this. Not as facts retrieved from memory, but as grammar.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood the impulse behind making a joke about the rebound relationship.
source_quote: I understood the impulse behind the joke.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz went quiet beside Zalthir around the second hour of walking — his hand went to his temple and stayed there.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet. His hand went to his temple and stayed there.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz's silence and hand-to-temple gesture were noticed by Zalthir — but Zalthir did not say anything yet.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet. His hand went to his temple and stayed there. I noticed. I didn't say anything yet.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, a dwarf with native understanding of Dwarven, noticed the Stroudite inscription on Tarvis Ulain’s monument and later experienced persistent pressure in his head, suggesting he is a secondary recipient of the same Underdark corruption affecting Elin.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Drow (Player Character)
fact: The drow has no memory of their past, suffers from a persistent headache, and was imprisoned in the Underdark with others before escaping. They are currently in Candlekeep, seeking help and truth, and have no knowledge of their identity or history. They are not lying, but cannot afford the usual drow strategies of concealment.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story. This is the short version. I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail. Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us. And we've made an escape. We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada. Now I'm here in Candlekeep. My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin is a 7-year-old girl who has been silent for six days, draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface in her environment, and speaks only in her sleep — her utterance being 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: She says it is only the shape that holds.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin spoke after Lesser Restoration: 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: And then she spoke. 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: Elin
fact: Elin, a 7-year-old girl from Maerith, has been silent for six days and compulsively draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface, while speaking in her sleep with the phrase 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface... She says it is only the shape that holds... 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: Festrum
fact: Festrum, the ancient gnome innkeeper of The Burning Wizard Inn, maintains the physical memory of a wizard's death by refusing to paint the wall where he fell, and scrubs the floor seasonally as ritual observance.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: Festrum
fact: Festrum, the gnome innkeeper, has maintained the Burning Wizard Inn for thirty years and remembers the story of the burned wizard.
source_quote: Festrum — the gnome innkeeper, old enough to have heard the story from the people who told it first — pointed to the south wall without prompting...

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool asked Zalthir directly: 'Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?' — and received an affirmative answer.
source_quote: Glabbagool paused, and asked me directly: "Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?"

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool committed to keeping an eye on the spy.
source_quote: I will keep an eye on her!

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool found the spy entertaining because she kept trying to kill him, and they had become great friends.
source_quote: He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream. He'd try to explain the way of the shadow and teach her meditation. She'd scream about the meditation. Then they'd talk. He said they'd become great friends.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is ambivalent about watching the spy.
source_quote: Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool took Zalthir's affirmation seriously and believed the work counted.
source_quote: Glabbagool took this with complete seriousness. The work counted; he had been told so.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool was glad to be asked about the spy's status.
source_quote: Glabbagool was glad to be asked.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a grey ooze, was carried in the same bag as the spy and had spent days observing and interacting with her; he claimed they had become great friends through repeated attempts at murder, escape, meditation, and conversation, and asked Zalthir whether this made him more or less of a monk.
source_quote: Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her?

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a sentient grey ooze, has been shaped by Zalthir’s guidance into an unlikely monk-in-training. He absorbs lessons through conflict, treating the spy’s attempts to kill him as spiritual exercises — his formlessness becoming a metaphor for adaptability.
source_quote: Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum arrived at Candlekeep and was assigned to Vareth; he was the one who first noted the connection between Daz’s distress and the spreading madness from the Underdark, and summarized the group’s capture as: "We've been caught."
source_quote: We've been caught.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Elin’s condition was interior and untouchable by conventional means.
source_quote: Whatever was happening inside Elin was interior in a way that made it untouchable through conventional means.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the Stroudite inscription on the monument was either ignored or tolerated.
source_quote: The priest conceded, looking left, looking right, like the Stroudites might be listening.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes something is wrong and tenuous with Daz's condition.
source_quote: He couldn't pin it down, he said. Something wrong, something tenuous.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes things have to be done with a grain of salt.
source_quote: These things have to be done with a grain of salt.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum dropped a gold piece for a pewter hand cast and asked the priest why the Stroudite inscription remained on a Bahamutian paladin's monument.
source_quote: Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his. Then Grygum asked him to tell him more — he'd already paid, so he had the leverage — and the priest was very willing. 'The inscription shares language with Stroud. Why is that?'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum filed the phenomenon under open questions and kept writing.
source_quote: I filed it under open questions and kept writing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum has a scholar's interest in Stroud that he performs slightly harder than the interest actually requires.
source_quote: Grygum leaned forward — he has a scholar's interest in Stroud that he performs slightly harder than the interest actually requires — and offered her a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is Bahamutian, with sentimentality for Stroud.
source_quote: he explained that he was Bahamutian, with sentimentality for the other.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut who notices and questions the layered symbolism of the monument, purchases a pewter hand cast, and presses the priest for theological clarity, revealing his role as an investigator of hidden truths.
source_quote: Grygum looked at them. 'Are they full size?'... Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his... Grygum asked him to tell him more... 'As am I,' Grygum said. 'But the inscription shares language with Stroud. Why is that?'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a scholar whose interest in Stroud is performed slightly harder than the interest actually requires — and he offered a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.
source_quote: Grygum leaned forward — he has a scholar's interest in Stroud that he performs slightly harder than the interest actually requires — and offered her a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a scholar whose interest in Stroud’s chess game is performed with exaggerated intensity, masking a deeper obsession with patterns of decay and forgotten doctrines. He collects anomalies like relics, noting their cadences and distortions with ritual precision.
source_quote: The only love I remember during the previous campaign," he said, "involved giants, and it wasn't Stroud's.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a scholar with a performative interest in Stroud, who maps thematic motifs from bardic songs onto historical figures like Whistler, and accepts theological downgrades with bureaucratic precision.
source_quote: The only love I remember during the previous campaign, involved giants, and it wasn't Stroud's.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the unnatural silence in Daggerford.
source_quote: Grygum noticed it too, I could tell, though he didn't say anything.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed that Whistler’s restraint mapped well onto his own philosophy.
source_quote: Grygum, who has an irritating habit of noticing things I would have preferred to notice first, observed drily that the song's principle — steal what was needed — mapped rather well onto Whistler.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled that the only love he remembers during the previous campaign involved giants, and it wasn't Stroud's.
source_quote: The only love I remember during the previous campaign," he said, "involved giants, and it wasn't Stroud's.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum still thinks about Zuggtmoy and probably will for the rest of his life.
source_quote: I still think about Zuggtmoy, and will probably continue thinking about Zuggtmoy for the rest of my life.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum suspected a tenuous connection between Elin’s condition and Daz’s headache.
source_quote: There's some kind of tenuous connection there?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was convinced the silence in Elin was not absence but insistence.
source_quote: Silence isn't absence. Seven years old and drawing the same thing on every flat surface is not nothing — it's insistence.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was quiet in a way that meant he was adding something to the list.
source_quote: Grygum was quiet. Not the usual quiet. The kind where he's adding something to the list.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum, a cleric of Bahamut, is deeply attuned to spiritual and metaphysical disturbances, documenting the connection between Elin's condition and Daz's headaches as evidence of a broader Underdark-induced perceptual breakdown.
source_quote: I took notes. Elin couldn't speak and Daz had a headache and somewhere below us the demon lords were apparently still broadcasting...

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the Gate Warden who laid out Candlekeep’s official policy on prisoners — and declared: 'We hold prisoners. We do not keep them.'
source_quote: Gate Warden. He was efficient about it. He laid out Candlekeep's position without apology: "... we hold prisoners. We do not keep them."

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, Gate Warden of Candlekeep, reviewed the group’s violation of protocol regarding the spy and delivered Candlekeep’s official stance: that prisoners are not kept, only delayed, and that the spy would be released eventually with a warning.
source_quote: What you are giving us is a delay.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire announced the award of a specialized shadow technique — three options, presented carefully, with the honest note that adjustments might be needed if any proved mechanically unfortunate.
source_quote: Although your skills are weak, clearly showing a lack of focus and training. There is something special about how you hit. The way of the Shadow is not about hitting. It is about discrete movement. And it is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire asked Zalthir: 'What were you sent toward? Not why were you sent here?' — and later stated: 'I will not be there. This is your work, not mine.'
source_quote: Khell-Vire opened with the question. "What were you sent toward? Not why were you sent here?" ... Then Khell-Vire set the terms clearly: "There are monks here in the inner ward who have read everything and fought nothing. They will want to test you. Let them. You will learn what you do not see, and they will learn what cannot be read. I will not be there. This is your work, not mine."

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a blind monk who initially judged Zalthir’s skills as weak and untrained, but ultimately recognized that Zalthir’s combination of shadow step and strike — not his individual mechanics — revealed a deeper, forgotten lineage of shadow monks, and awarded him a specialized technique as a result.
source_quote: There is something special about how you hit. The way of the Shadow is not about hitting. It is about discrete movement.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a master of shadow monkery who recognized that Zalthir’s unorthodox method — though violating the manual — embodies the true philosophy of the shadow: movement over force, combination over conformity.
source_quote: There is something special about how you hit. The way of the Shadow is not about hitting. It is about discrete movement.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a perceptive shadow master who recognized that Zalthir’s unorthodox technique — born of disregard for the manual — is the true innovation in shadow monkery, and offered him a specialized technique in acknowledgment.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a two-hundred-year-old half-elf shadow monk who refused an order decades ago and now serves as a silent archivist of forgotten lineages. He tests others not to judge their skill, but to reveal what they have become through their choices.
source_quote: This question is for you, not for me.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a two-hundred-year-old half-elven shadow monk lineage keeper who evaluates students not on what they know, but on what they have become through lived experience; he operates outside traditional pedagogical frameworks.
source_quote: He was asking what Zalthir had become through what he'd lived.

subject: Librarian (Menzoberranzan Scholar)
fact: The librarian is a scholar of drow noble houses with access to sealed records. She understands the mechanics of power, betrayal, and record manipulation in Menzoberranzan. She trusts the drow’s honesty despite its deviation from cultural norms and guides them through the hidden logic of the Houses, especially the meaning of 'struck' and the privileges of the fourth seat.
source_quote: Whenever a house sought to destroy another house, it had to destroy everyone. If you left a single person alive — even a child, even someone inconvenient and useless — your house was forfeit. The wider community would come for you. They would reduce you to a black puddle and call the matter settled.

subject: Maerith of the Ford
fact: Maerith is Elin’s mother, exhausted from seeking help at every temple and institution, and has repeatedly been turned away — she noticed the dragon-and-scale holy symbol as the usual trigger for hope.
source_quote: She spotted my holy symbol during dinner, which is the usual trigger.

subject: Master Archivist Philemon
fact: Master Archivist Philemon was assigned as Thorin's handler at Candlekeep — without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony. Thorin to Master Archivist Philemon.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is the head of a publisher affiliated with the Order of the Gauntlet and personally witnessed and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, signing off on its creation.
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the back. Common. *Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.* Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is the head of a publisher and a member of the Order of the Gauntlet who personally witnessed and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, signing it with the phrase 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.'
source_quote: The smaller inscription on the back read: 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.' Signed by Milo Goodbarrel.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel, head of a publisher and member of the Order of the Gauntlet, personally signed the monument's inscription.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet. Milo had personally signed off on this.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator has seen this pattern of degradation before — twice — in Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher.
source_quote: I have seen it before. Twice. Eldred had it, earlier in the journey — the man who went insane. The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator knows the chant well enough to know what the scholar was doing wrong.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong,

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator understands that the wall remembers better than he would like to.
source_quote: I find I understand that better than I would like to.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon confirmed we were enrolled in a two-stage process, and accepted the way I accept most things I've already decided to do: by not arguing about it.
source_quote: She can't be polished, actually.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is a master archivist who shifted from viewing Dawnbringer as a specimen to recognizing her as a sentient being with emotional trauma, and adapted his approach to honor her personhood.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is an archivist trained to view magical artifacts as specimens, but he paused and reset his assumptions when confronted with Thorin’s insistence on Dawnbringer’s personhood — indicating a latent openness to redefining classification beyond institutional norms.
source_quote: He looked up. There was a pause. The kind where someone resets the question in their head before they say the next thing.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is not offended by flippant remarks about sentient weapons and has likely heard worse, demonstrating emotional resilience and familiarity with magical artifacts.
source_quote: I understand," Philemon said. He wasn't offended. He'd probably heard worse.

subject: Priest of Bahamut
fact: The priest claimed to be a pure Bahamutian and conceded the inscription was a gift left in place because Tarvis saved everyone regardless of the chess game.
source_quote: He himself was, he wanted us to know, *a pure Bahamutian*. He did not believe in the heresy. 'It was a gift,' he said finally. 'And since it was a gift, we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?'

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne is a Candlekeep Avowed who enforces reciprocal knowledge exchange with quiet authority, and was visibly unsettled yet convinced by Daz’s unprecedented honesty.
source_quote: Wow, that's quite a bit.

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne is a Candlekeep archivist who manages scholarly inquiries with patient, unwavering adherence to protocol, accustomed to unorthodox requests from overeager researchers.
source_quote: Sister Yvenne looked at me with the particular expression of someone who has spent decades managing scholars and has nevertheless not encountered this exact request.

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne was assigned as Daz's handler at Candlekeep — without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony. Daz to Sister Yvenne.

subject: Spy
fact: The spy is furious about being treated as a guest rather than a prisoner.
source_quote: The spy, for her part, was furious.

subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a paladin of Bahamut who died three years ago in Daggerford while breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation. His severed bronze forearm is mounted on a stone pillar as a monument, bearing a Stroudite inscription and signed by Milo Goodbarrel of the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: The primary inscription read: 'Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.'

subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a paladin of Bahamut who died three years ago in Daggerford while breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation. His severed bronze forearm is mounted on a stone pillar as a monument, bearing inscriptions in Common, Dwarven, and a reference to Stroudite chess symbolism.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription. The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years, died in Daggerford breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The Blind Monk is a senior shadow monk evaluator who enforces canonical techniques but is forced to acknowledge superior efficacy in unorthodox methods; he represents institutional dogma confronted by adaptive mastery.
source_quote: You skip the third breath... It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did.

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk is an examiner bound by tradition, judging Zalthir by scrolls that no longer apply. His rigid metrics fail to account for survival-based mastery — yet he recognizes Zalthir’s power, even as he cannot name it.
source_quote: You have learned nothing.

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk told Zalthir after his failed demonstrations: 'You have learned nothing.'
source_quote: He rolled catastrophically. He fell. The monk watched him fall — insofar as a blind man watches anything — and said, without apparent emotion: "You have learned nothing."

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk told Zalthir: 'You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did. Show me what else you haven't learned.'
source_quote: The blind monk entered without introduction and said: "Give me a standard shadow step." ... Then he paused. "You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did. Show me what else you haven't learned."

subject: The monk
fact: The monk thought perhaps he'd been approaching this the wrong way.
source_quote: Perhaps I've been approaching this the wrong way.

subject: The monk
fact: The monk was, by every available indication, genuinely impressed.
source_quote: He was, by every available indication, genuinely impressed.

subject: The Spy (House T'sarran)
fact: The spy, a miniaturized operative of House T'sarran, was discovered in the group’s bag at Candlekeep’s gate; she demanded formal imprisonment and was furious when told her fate was not hers to decide, but she had become an unwilling companion to Glabbagool.
source_quote: I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed.

subject: The Spy (Miniaturized House T'sarran Operative)
fact: The spy is a prisoner who demands incarceration not for safety, but for legitimacy — she wants to be seen as a captive of authority, not a burden carried by adventurers. Her fury stems from being treated as a tool rather than a person.
source_quote: I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: The Traveling Bard
fact: A traveling bard performs seasonal songs with thematic resonance — including 'The Kenku Could Not Fly' — and adapts her repertoire in response to patrons' holy symbols, translating grand theological narratives into accessible folk metaphors.
source_quote: She took the coin and proceeded to sing a love song. Involving flowers. And drinking.

subject: The Young Human Scholar
fact: A young human scholar in the corner of The Burning Wizard Inn is reciting a liturgical chant with a precise, non-beginner-level degradation pattern — identical to the cognitive distortions previously observed in Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher.
source_quote: His breathing was almost right. The pauses fell almost correctly. The pattern was almost the one it was supposed to be — and wrong by a hair in a way that took actual knowledge of the correct version to notice.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin arrived at Candlekeep and was assigned to Master Archivist Philemon; he processed the group’s ethical dilemma by talking to Glabbagool and concluded the ooze was ambivalent about its role as a jailer.
source_quote: You just gotta go with it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asked whether Glabbagool had thoughts on the matter — and observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.
source_quote: Thorin, who processes things by talking, asked whether Glabbagool had thoughts on the matter. ... Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes life takes you in weird directions and weird places, and you just gotta go with it.
source_quote: Life takes you in weird directions and weird places," he said. "You just gotta go with it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin came back in with the settled look of a man who had had a thought that satisfied him.
source_quote: He came back in with the settled look of a man who had had a thought that satisfied him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin found the sight of Dawnbringer lighting up the sea peaceful rather than counterproductive.
source_quote: Thorin apparently found this peaceful rather than counterproductive, which I note without judgment.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a companion who advocates for Dawnbringer’s personhood, insists on using gendered pronouns for a sentient blade, and seeks validation for the emotional bond formed through shared trauma — challenging institutional dehumanization of magical artifacts.
source_quote: What do you mean, specimen? This is my friend Dawnbringer.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a companion who provides blunt, humorous commentary — notably naming the 'Pocket Drow' — and serves as a grounding voice amid surreal and philosophical developments.
source_quote: Pocket Drow.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the silence in Daggerford wasn't natural.
source_quote: The hill giants I grew up with — they had a word for a silence that wasn't natural.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin processes the world through conversation and observation, often revealing hidden truths by asking the wrong questions. He accepts paradoxes as natural — whether it’s a sentient ooze becoming a monk or the sea being defeated by light — and finds peace in surrender rather than resolution.
source_quote: Life takes you in weird directions and weird places," he said. "You just gotta go with it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin referred to the drow as 'Pocket Drow.'
source_quote: Pocket Drow.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin stared at the bronze forearm monument longer than he should have.
source_quote: I stared at it for longer than I should have.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin stopped counting days and started counting how much his boots hurt.
source_quote: We'd been on the road south out of the Silver Marches long enough that I'd stopped counting days and started counting how much my boots hurt.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought about how many towns north of Daggerford had similar stories but hadn't put up monuments.
source_quote: I stood in the doorway of the River Shining and thought about how many towns north of here had a story like this, and just hadn't put up a bronze arm about it yet.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to make sure he hadn't misread the Dwarven inscription.
source_quote: I read it twice because Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin was satisfied that the gelatinous cube had not been dismissed as a mindless digestive system.
source_quote: I noted with some satisfaction that we had not brought a gelatinous cube this far — through the Underdark, through Waterdeep, into the libraries of Candlekeep — to have him dismissed as a mindless digestive system before lunch.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin watched a woman cross the road to avoid a conversation and then pretend she hadn't.
source_quote: I watched a woman cross the road to avoid a conversation and then pretend she hadn't.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth was assigned as Grygum's handler at Candlekeep — without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony. Grygum to Vareth.

subject: Whistler
fact: Whistler, the Kenku thief, took only what was necessary from Tiamat’s hoard, forming a line-item budget.
source_quote: The Kenku thief of some earlier age who, presented with the complete hoard of Tiamat, had apparently taken only what was necessary for legitimate expenses. Operating goals. Day-to-day funds. Per diems.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne is a custodian of restricted knowledge in Menzoberranzan, maintaining the public record's appearance while withholding truths beyond its scope, her physical stillness betraying deliberate concealment.
source_quote: Yvenne’s body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne is a keeper of restricted knowledge in Menzoberranzan, maintaining a pose of neutral informant while her body language — five minutes of practiced stillness contradicting her words — reveals she is carefully navigating what she can say, knowing more than the public record allows.
source_quote: She had been sitting for the last several minutes — the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne maintains a practiced stillness inconsistent with her words, indicating she knows more than the public record allows her to say and is carefully navigating rather than simply informing.
source_quote: Yvenne's body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes. The practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne maintains the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say.
source_quote: the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir acknowledged that the shadow monks had driven him nuts.
source_quote: Yeah, definitely.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir arrived at Candlekeep and was assigned to Brother Khell-Vire as his handler, having previously meditated on the roof and resolved an internal argument about the nature of wisdom and delay.
source_quote: Hmm, true,

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed he had built something better than the manual.
source_quote: He was now being told that the thing he'd built was the most interesting thing about him.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir found the manual aggravating and ignored it.
source_quote: Zalthir found the manual aggravating, ignored it, and built something better.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had played this game before — the shadow monk pedagogy — and found it annoying.
source_quote: I've played this game before, my friends," Zalthir said, which was directed at no one in particular, or possibly at us, or possibly at the entire tradition of shadow monk pedagogy stretching back five centuries.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified the mechanism of Elin’s condition as a perceptual distortion — the world is arriving as corrupted audio input she cannot process, not as magic or disease.
source_quote: The input, the audio, the way the world was arriving at her rather than the world itself.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combat-optimized individual who ignored the manual, built an unconventional shadow technique through improvisation, and impressed the blind monk Khell-Vire with a 29-to-hit strike that shattered a thrown brick — demonstrating that his unorthodox approach is more effective than traditional training.
source_quote: I rolled a 29 to hit. The brick did not survive.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combatant who ignored the manual, built a unique shadow-step-and-hit technique, and now embodies the most interesting aspect of shadow monkery — his combination of movement and strike redeems his lack of traditional skills.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a shadow monk who disregarded formal training in favor of practical survival in the Underdark; he executes techniques unconventionally but effectively, prioritizing results over doctrinal correctness.
source_quote: He had survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a shadow monk who survived the Underdark through unconventional means, rejecting formal training in favor of what works. He now navigates Candlekeep’s rigid traditions with quiet defiance, recognizing that his deviations are not errors but adaptations.
source_quote: Absolutely," I said. It was. Patience under provocation. Maintaining stillness when the environment is actively hostile. Responding to aggression without being ruled by it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by Khell-Vire as the one who built something better in spite of the manual, and whose combination of shadow step and hit is the most interesting thing about him.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the one who confirmed to Glabbagool that watching the spy is pre-monk training — and Glabbagool accepted the assignment with complete seriousness.
source_quote: "Absolutely," I said. It was. Patience under provocation. Maintaining stillness when the environment is actively hostile. Responding to aggression without being ruled by it. If anything, the spy was giving him a better curriculum than most of what I'd sat through. Glabbagool took this with complete seriousness.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled a moment from the Underdark where he'd found a way to punch through the shadows themselves.
source_quote: Zalthir recalled something from the Underdark — a moment where he'd found a way to punch *through* the shadows themselves

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said 'Hmm, true,' in the tone of a man completing an internal argument rather than beginning an external one.
source_quote: He said "Hmm, true," about something, in the tone of a man completing an internal argument rather than beginning an external one.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said to Glabbagool: 'Absolutely' — confirming that watching the spy was pre-monk training.
source_quote: "Absolutely," I said. It was. Patience under provocation. Maintaining stillness when the environment is actively hostile. Responding to aggression without being ruled by it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said to the blind monk: 'I mean, I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?' — after Thorin asked if he could blindside the monk while walking away.
source_quote: Thorin, from the side: "Can he attack him while he's walking away? Blindside him, as it were?" Zalthir: "I mean, I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?"

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said: 'I've played this game before, my friends' — referring to shadow monk pedagogy stretching back five centuries.
source_quote: "I've played this game before, my friends," Zalthir said, which was directed at no one in particular, or possibly at us, or possibly at the entire tradition of shadow monk pedagogy stretching back five centuries.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir, a Dragonborn, identified the mechanism behind Elin’s condition as non-magical perceptual distortion — the world arriving as an unprocessable language — and contributed critical analysis to the group’s understanding of the phenomenon.
source_quote: Zalthir articulated the mechanism: the input, the audio, the way the world was arriving at her rather than the world itself.

subject: bronze-cast forearm
fact: A bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar, not holding anything.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar. Not holding anything. Just a hand.

subject: bronze forearm monument
fact: The bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain is a severed, mounted limb with no weapon, bearing a Dwarven Stroudite inscription ('The move is yours') and a Common Gauntlet record, symbolizing the collision of faiths and forgotten histories.
source_quote: A bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar. Not holding anything. Just a hand.

subject: bronze forearm monument
fact: The bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain is mounted on a stone pillar in Daggerford’s market square, bearing three inscriptions: Common (identifying Tarvis), Dwarven (*The move is yours.*), and Common (*Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.*).
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Clay Tablet
fact: Philemon’s clay tablet was used to record Dawnbringer as a specimen — later abandoned when he recognized her as a sentient being — symbolizing the shift from objectification to personhood.
source_quote: He had a small clay tablet ready. He was already writing... He set the tablet down.

subject: Common inscription
fact: The Common inscription on the back reads: 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.' Signed by Milo Goodbarrel.
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the back. Common. *Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.* Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a named sunblade weapon that requires not physical maintenance but spiritual reconnection to light and emotional mourning for past trauma.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer, the sentient sword, performed Lesser Restoration on Elin, enabling her speech.
source_quote: Dawnbringer could help. Dawnbringer did not wait for a second invitation. 'Let me bring the light to you.' Lesser restoration settled in.

subject: Daz name origin
fact: It is possible my name, Daz, is a shortened form of Daz'issin — a name my mother may have used, implying a protective diminutive.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did. I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used. She redirected. Let us turn to your patron, she said.

subject: Daz's Journal
fact: Daz's journal contains precise transcriptions of the malformed chant cadence, including syncopation errors and syllabic deviations — data he intends to cross-reference with Candlekeep’s archives to determine if this is a known doctrine or an emerging corruption.
source_quote: Candlekeep would have records. Someone there would know whether this pattern belonged to a group, a practice, a doctrine — or whether it was something else being made to look like one.

subject: Dwarven inscription
fact: The Dwarven inscription on the base reads: 'The move is yours.'
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the base. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: evidence of fungal infection
fact: There was no evidence of fungal infection in Elin's condition.
source_quote: Is there any evidence of any sort of fungal infection? No. No.

subject: evidence of the six-pointed star
fact: Elin drew a six-pointed star on every flat surface.
source_quote: a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house.

subject: evidence of the world speaking a new language
fact: The world had started speaking a language Elin couldn't process.
source_quote: the world had started speaking a language she couldn't process

subject: Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldic text, deliberately defaced by a razor cut removing an appendix referenced in a footnote, which contained the only known record of Daz'issin’s full lineage and context.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldry book with a mechanically removed appendix that referenced a footnote about Daz'issin.
source_quote: Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe. Two hundred years old, give or take. The footnote referenced an appendix. The appendix was missing. I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor.

subject: Heraldry book: *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe*
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldic text, partially defaced by a deliberate, razor-cut removal of an appendix referenced by a footnote on Daz'issin, indicating intentional suppression of information tied to the name and its lineage.
source_quote: A razor. Not age, not water damage, not the slow forgetting of paper that has been handled too many times. A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: inscription signer
fact: Milo Goodbarrel signed the inscription 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.'
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: kenku thief principle
fact: Whistler took only what was necessary from Tiamat's hoard.
source_quote: Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget.

subject: Khell-Vire's note
