source_quote: Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.

subject: Note on Khell-Vire's Desk
fact: The note — 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings' — is an enigmatic directive with no known origin, serving as a cryptic trigger for the trial’s philosophical inquiry into meaning, memory, and lived experience.
source_quote: Neither of them could place it. I filed it under 'questions to revisit' and did not volunteer an opinion, because I didn't have one.

subject: pewter hand cast
fact: Pewter miniature replicas of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm are being sold by a village priest as charitable donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, measuring charm-sized and not full size.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway... carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: pewter hand casts
fact: Miniature pewter reproductions of Tarvis Ulain’s severed hand are sold as charms by a priest, marketed as donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, and perceived as grotesque souvenirs by the party.
source_quote: Small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: pewter hand casts
fact: Small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, charm-sized, sold for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway — walking in very pleased with himself and carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized. He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: pewter hand cast value
fact: The pewter hand casts are charm-sized and sold for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: Pocket Drow
fact: Pocket Drow is a small, living drow kept by Thorin — a symbolic and possibly sentient companion that represents the unexpected, non-threatening presence of drow culture outside Menzoberranzan’s violent norms.
source_quote: Pocket Drow.

subject: Pocket Drow
fact: Thorin, helpfully: 'Pocket Drow.'
source_quote: Thorin, helpfully: 'Pocket Drow.'

subject: Resonant Slime
fact: Resonant Slime is a magical vial produced by a xenobiology sage after observing the sentient gelatinous cube’s progress — used to affirm its sentience and potential as a student.
source_quote: Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: Resonant Slime
fact: Resonant Slime is a rare alchemical substance produced by the Gelatinous Cube Collective, used to affirm its sentience and legitimacy — its presence signifies institutional recognition of non-human intelligence.
source_quote: The sage... produced a vial of Resonant Slime.

subject: Resonant Slime
fact: The sage produced a vial of Resonant Slime. Glabbagool was very pleased.
source_quote: The sage produced a vial of Resonant Slime.

subject: Resonant Slime value
fact: The vial of Resonant Slime produced by the sage contains 10 milliliters of stabilized eldritch gel.
source_quote: produced a vial of Resonant Slime

subject: shadow technique value
fact: The specialized shadow technique chosen by Zalthir is option C, with potential mechanical adjustments.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C

subject: Shadow Tentacles
fact: Shadow Tentacles are an unrecorded, self-developed ability of Zalthir, grown from his eldritch tattoo — a technique outside official manuals, born of improvisation and later validated by Khell-Vire as a legitimate expression of shadow mastery.
source_quote: I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: shadow tentacle value
fact: The shadow tentacles grown by Zalthir are a result of eldritch tattoo augmentation, not innate ability.
source_quote: I learned how to grow shadow tentacles

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: six-pointed star
fact: Elin draws a six-pointed star over and over on every flat surface in her home.
source_quote: Yes, she'd noted the drawings — a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house.

subject: six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin’s compulsive drawings of a six-pointed star on every flat surface are a non-verbal communication of her perceptual breakdown, possibly representing a corrupted concept of 'wells' or divine access points.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface... a six-pointed star, over and over.

subject: Six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin’s repeated drawings of a six-pointed star on every flat surface are not random — they are an attempt to externalize and stabilize an internal perceptual collapse.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: struck count
fact: A struck fourth seat is not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price and having the infrastructure to make the payment look like it was never made.
source_quote: the fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records. That a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price and having the infrastructure to make the payment look like it was never made.

subject: sunblade value
fact: Dawnbringer, the sunblade, requires exposure to daylight and mourning for full restoration.
source_quote: She needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then... she needs to grieve.

subject: tarvis ulain's bronze arm
fact: Tarvis Ulain's bronze arm was severed at the elbow and mounted on a stone pillar.
source_quote: a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar.

subject: The Bag
fact: The bag contained both Glabbagool and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy; its contents were revealed at Candlekeep’s gate, triggering a protocol breach and forcing the party to confront the ethical implications of carrying a living prisoner and a monster together.
source_quote: We've been caught.

subject: The Kenku Could Not Fly
fact: The bard's song 'The Kenku Could Not Fly' includes the lyric: 'The raven thief who learned to steal no more, save what was needed.'
source_quote: This one was called 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.'... 'The raven thief who learned to steal no more, save what was needed, said the small, wise man at his side.'

subject: The Ledger of Houses
fact: A document listing the noble houses of Menzoberranzan, annotated with terms like 'second seat', 'fourth seat struck', 'eleventh seat', and 'twenty-third seat'. The term 'struck' is distinct from elimination — it implies attempted erasure that failed or was concealed. The document is held in Candlekeep and contains hidden meaning accessible only to those who understand Menzoberranzan's linguistic and bureaucratic codes.
source_quote: She read me the list. The second seat. The fourth seat struck. The eleventh seat. The twenty-third seat. *Struck.*

subject: The Miniaturized House T'sarran Spy
fact: A tiny, sentient spy from House T'sarran, magically reduced and carried in a bag with Glabbagool. She is not merely a tool but a being who demands recognition — her captivity is psychological as much as physical, and her fury stems from being treated as an object.
source_quote: I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: The Note on Khell-Vire's Desk
fact: The note on Khell-Vire's desk reads: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.' — neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire could place it.
source_quote: On Khell-Vire's desk, visible from where I was standing: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.* Zalthir stared at it. Khell-Vire stared at it. Neither of them could place it.

subject: The prescription
fact: A prescription is nearly retrieved by Philemon before he catches himself, suggesting an unspoken medical or magical intervention related to Dawnbringer’s condition or the narrator’s distress.
source_quote: He started to reach for a prescription and caught himself mid-sentence.

subject: The Shadow Monk Under-Robe
fact: Khell-Vire wears a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath his Candlekeep gray — a silent declaration that identity outlasts institution. It is not a relic, but a living memory, worn like skin.
source_quote: You don't stop dressing like what you were. You just layer something else over it.

subject: The Shadow Monk Under-Robe
fact: Khell-Vire wore a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray — a sign he had not stopped dressing like what he was.
source_quote: He wore a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray, which told me more about him than the records would have. You don't stop dressing like what you were. You just layer something else over it.

subject: The Spy's Attempted Murder of Glabbagool
fact: The spy kept trying to kill Glabbagool — he'd slap her around, she'd try to run, he'd expand, she'd scream, he'd try to explain the way of the shadow and teach her meditation — she'd scream about the meditation.
source_quote: She kept trying to kill him. He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream. He'd try to explain the way of the shadow and teach her meditation. She'd scream about the meditation.

subject: The Spy's Bag
fact: The bag contained Glabbagool and a miniaturized House T'sarran spy — which Gate Warden Kalan Strongbranch found unacceptable.
source_quote: When we'd come through the gate, we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him, which she apparently found unacceptable.

subject: wall's memory
fact: The south wall of the Burning Wizard Inn remembers where the wizard was burned.
source_quote: My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: Cognitive Contagion
fact: A recurring, identifiable distortion in ritual chanting may be a symptom of a broader, unexplained phenomenon — possibly tied to demon lord broadcasts or a hidden heresy — that has afflicted at least three people and may be spreading.
source_quote: I have seen it before. Twice.

subject: Daggerford's silent trauma
fact: Daggerford bears visible markers of war — the monument, the pewter relics, the lingering tension over religious symbolism — yet avoids open discussion of its pain, mirroring the unspoken silence observed by the party upon arrival.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense... Townfolk walked around something none of them would point at. Nobody explained why.

subject: Dawnbringer's first wielder
fact: Dawnbringer’s silence upon being asked about her previous wielder suggests deep trauma tied to a death or betrayal — one that may be central to her need to grieve, and which remains unspoken.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: The full identity and history of Daz'issin is missing, as the appendix referenced by the footnote was deliberately removed with a razor.
source_quote: I found a footnote instead... The appendix was missing. I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor.

subject: Daz's headache and Elin's silence
fact: Daz’s persistent head pressure and Elin’s inability to speak may be symptoms of the same phenomenon — an external, non-magical corruption that disrupts how the world is received — suggesting a shared, unexplained vulnerability among those attuned to deeper truths.
source_quote: I looked at him. I looked at Elin. I thought about what we'd just established: that something from below was bleeding up...

subject: Daz's identity
fact: Daz is a potential survivor of a wiped-out Menzoberranzan house — the 'blithering idiot' — and his amnesia, headache, and drow heritage may be linked to a forbidden legacy the city tried to erase.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Daz's origin
fact: The possibility that Daz's name is a maternal diminutive from a lost house remains unverified and unspoken.
source_quote: She told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries. And that the houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Daz's origins
fact: Daz does not know why his head hurts or who he was before being imprisoned.
source_quote: I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Daz's past
fact: Daz's memory of his life before imprisonment is missing.
source_quote: I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail.

subject: Glabbagool’s monkhood
fact: Glabbagool’s interaction with the spy has raised a metaphysical question: whether watching and engaging with a prisoner constitutes spiritual growth or moral corruption; Zalthir affirmed it as pre-monk training, but the nature of that training remains ambiguous.
source_quote: Absolutely.

subject: Is Wisdom the Same as Resignation?
fact: Thorin’s statement — 'You just gotta go with it' — haunts the party. Is it acceptance? Or surrender? The line blurs in Candlekeep, where knowledge is preserved, but change is deferred — and the only certainty is that some things will never be solved.
source_quote: I have not yet decided whether it is wisdom or resignation. Possibly there is not much difference.

subject: Manual vs. Improvisation
fact: The ongoing conflict between official combat manuals and Zalthir’s self-built techniques continues to produce results that invalidate the manuals — a thread that redefines mastery as creation rather than conformity.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: Missing appendix on Daz'issin
fact: The appendix referenced in the footnote on Daz'issin has been physically excised from the heraldry book, creating an unresolved gap in the historical record that may contain the truth of Daz's origins, the fate of his house, or the identity of his protector.
source_quote: The appendix was missing.

subject: priest's ambiguous tolerance
fact: The village priest claims to be a 'pure Bahamutian' but allows a Stroudite inscription to remain on the monument, citing it as a 'gift' that should not be removed, suggesting deeper political or theological compromises.
source_quote: It was a gift,' he said finally. 'And since it was a gift, we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?'

subject: Pronoun of Dawnbringer
fact: The question of whether Dawnbringer is 'he,' 'she,' or 'they' remains unresolved in institutional records — but Thorin’s insistence on personhood has turned it into a living, unresolved ethical thread that challenges archival norms.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but... we've gotten to know each other pretty well.

subject: Shadow Monk Doctrine Failure
fact: The official shadow monk manual is fundamentally wrong about Zalthir — his unorthodox technique, built in spite of it, proves that true mastery arises not from adherence but from innovation — a systemic failure of the tradition.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Stroudite chess reference (*The move is yours.*) appears on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin, raising questions about religious syncretism, tolerance, or hidden alliances in post-war Daggerford.
source_quote: Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin in a town I'd barely heard of, and whoever commissioned it had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: The presence of a Stroudite chess reference ('The move is yours') on a Bahamutian paladin’s monument in Daggerford suggests a hidden, unacknowledged alliance or ideological overlap between the two faiths, raising theological and political questions.
source_quote: Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin in a town I'd barely heard of...

subject: The Bleeding Underdark
fact: The structural wrongness from beneath is not contained — it is rising, affecting perception across the surface world, and may be the root cause of recent phenomena in Neverlight Grove, the Pudding King’s court, and now Elin.
source_quote: It was reaching up. It was reaching Elin.

subject: The Blithering Child Survivor
fact: The identity of the child who survived the house purge is unknown. The drow asks if they are that child — a question the librarian refuses to answer directly. The silence implies the drow may be the survivor, and their memory loss, headache, and presence in Candlekeep are not coincidences but consequences of a cover-up.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: The 'blithering idiot' legacy
fact: Menzoberranzan’s doctrine requires total annihilation of rival houses — yet one survivor, a 'blithering idiot,' escaped and may now be Daz — a living anomaly that challenges the city’s control over memory and history.
source_quote: Unclear... Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: The Chant of the Field Ward Preacher
fact: A rhythmic, liturgical chant — identical to one previously heard from Eldred (the madman) and the Field Ward Preacher — is being recited by a young scholar in Candlekeep. Its cadence is subtly corrupted, suggesting a spreading pattern of psychic decay or ritual corruption tied to the Underdark’s madness.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong.

subject: The combination of shadow step and hit
fact: The way forward was in the combination.
source_quote: Then he said the way forward was in the combination.

subject: The Curriculum Divide
fact: The central unresolved thread is whether formal monastic training and survival-based adaptation are mutually exclusive, or if one is merely a subset of the other — a question neither institution nor individual can fully answer.
source_quote: There's a case to be made that those are the same thing. There's also a case that they're almost never the same thing.

subject: The Difference Between Solutions and Postponements
fact: A lesson from Candlekeep’s monastery — remembered only in fragments — suggests that many acts of justice are not resolutions but delays. Zalthir now lives this truth: keeping the spy is not saving her, but postponing her fate.
source_quote: I remember nothing else from that class. I remember wanting to be in the training hall.

subject: The first wielder's identity
fact: The identity of Dawnbringer’s original wielder — the corpse she was found in — remains unspoken but deeply significant, and its unasked question lingers in the silence after Dawnbringer goes quiet.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind.

subject: The giants' saying
fact: The narrator’s childhood giants had a saying: 'the ground under a joker is the same ground everyone else is standing on' — a metaphor for humor as a response to unbearable specificity, now echoed in their own flippant remarks.
source_quote: The giants who raised me had a saying that translated roughly as: the ground under a joker is the same ground everyone else is standing on.

subject: The Headache
fact: Daz’s persistent headache may be a psychic echo of Menzoberranzan’s erased memories — a haunting residue of the house that was wiped out, and of the identity he was meant to forget.
source_quote: My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: The Manual Was Wrong
fact: The official shadow monk manual failed to account for Zalthir’s innovation — proving that the most powerful expressions of the tradition arise not from adherence, but from rebellion and synthesis.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: The Missing Appendix
fact: The appendix referenced in the footnote of the heraldic text was physically excised — a deliberate act of historical sabotage — leaving no record of Daz'issin’s true identity, lineage, or the circumstances of his family’s destruction.
source_quote: The footnote referenced an appendix. The appendix was missing.

subject: The Note: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.'
fact: A cryptic note on Khell-Vire’s desk references Zalthir’s journey and an unknown entity — the Bone King — whose singing may mark an impending event. Neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire can place it, but its presence suggests a hidden lineage or prophecy tied to the Underdark’s collapse.
source_quote: Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.

subject: The plus one
fact: The narrator jokingly suggests Dawnbringer will 'grow a plus one' — implying a future companion or evolution — a hopeful, informal closure to a heavy narrative arc.
source_quote: We're all gonna grow out of this," I said. "Hopefully, Dawnbringer grows a plus one.

subject: The Pressure in Daz’s Head
fact: Daz’s unacknowledged head pressure suggests he is experiencing the same perceptual bleed as Elin — a sign the corruption is spreading and may be active in others.
source_quote: I looked at him. I looked at Elin. I thought about what we'd just established.

subject: The Sealed Record
fact: There is a house so deeply erased that even the librarian cannot speak of it within the library — because the public record is sealed, and she is the public record. To uncover the truth, the drow must seek it through other doors, suggesting the existence of hidden archives, illicit networks, or non-recorded histories outside Candlekeep’s official collection.
source_quote: There was one house she could not speak of in the room. Not because she would not — because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: the spreading madness
fact: Daz’s uncharacteristic silence and distress suggest the Underdark’s spreading madness has followed the party to Candlekeep; its origin, mechanism, and target remain unknown, and it may be more than mere psychological trauma.
source_quote: Something wrong, something tenuous.

subject: the spy’s fate
fact: The fate of the House T'sarran spy remains unresolved: Candlekeep refuses to execute or imprison her, but will not release her immediately; the party must decide whether to accept a delay, intervene, or abandon her — a question that echoes the difference between solutions and postponements.
source_quote: What you are giving us is a delay.

subject: The Struck Fourth Seat
fact: The identity and fate of the house associated with the 'struck' fourth seat remain obscured. The term implies an attempted erasure that did not fully succeed, and the drow suspects they are connected to it — possibly as the sole survivor. The record was altered using archive privileges, and the truth is buried under layers of institutional deception.
source_quote: Struck," I said. "Didn't mean eliminated. It means they struck it, but maybe they didn't eliminate it, and therefore, like, it didn't happen? Is that why I feel like it's different?

subject: The truth-telling exchange in the Hall of Divination
fact: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: The two-stage process for Dawnbringer
fact: The first work is light. The second work is mourning.
source_quote: The first work is light. The second work is mourning.

subject: The Way of the Shadow
fact: The Way of the Shadow is not about hitting — it is about discrete movement — and Zalthir’s combination of shadow step and strike, though unorthodox, proves he has internalized its true essence.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas.

subject: The Wells Are Not Wells Anymore
fact: Elin’s utterance is a cryptic revelation pointing to a fundamental distortion in reality — 'wells' may symbolize sources of perception, truth, or connection that have been corrupted or replaced.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: Thorin's belief
fact: The narrator has not yet decided whether Thorin's statement is wisdom or resignation, and suspects there may not be much difference.
source_quote: I have been thinking about that sentence since he said it. I have not yet decided whether it is wisdom or resignation. Possibly there is not much difference.

subject: Underdark perceptual bleed
fact: A non-magical, systemic corruption from the Underdark is affecting surface dwellers’ perception, causing hallucinations, silence, and headaches, implying the demon lords are no longer confined below and are rewriting reality’s language.
source_quote: The madness from the Underdark... was not, apparently, staying below. It was reaching up.
